Generalize the pair into one helper, for example `func isLive<Node: NodeState>(_ type: Node.Type, at slot: Int) -> Bool`, and have `isLiveTask`, `isLiveActor`, and the TagMarkers check call it. Only the node type differs (ActorNode instead of TaskNode). The two copies can drift apart, so a later change to the liveness rule could fix one and miss the other. Make one shared liveness helper that takes the node type as a generic parameter, for example `func isLive<N: NodeState>(at slot: Int, as type: N.Type) -> Bool`, and have isLiveActor call it with ActorNode.self. Do not edit Readiness.swift:323 in this change. Report the switch of isLiveTask to the shared helper as a separate task.

Two copies of this helper must now be kept in step, and a fix to one will not reach the other. Move the helper to one shared place in the test support files, such as a `KanbanGraphTests` or `ColumnActorTests` extension, and call it from both suites. Remove the copy in RustFieldTests.swift.
